confirmed.title: A deleted step type cascade-deletes steps on trashed rugs outside the pass, leaving RugCostTotal stale
confirmed.scenario: Reproduced on a throwaway DB. Setup: a tenant step type X is used only on rug R, which has a Completed step of type X costing 1,000,000. R is then moved to the trash. A Configure user deletes X. The usage check at :123 runs `rugSteps.ListAsync`, which applies the RugWorkflowStep query filter `s.Rug.DeletedAt == null`. That filter hides R's step, so the count is 0 and :136 hard-deletes the type. ProcessStepType is not a watched type, so the save takes the fast path. The database FK cascade (RugWorkflowSteps.ProcessStepTypeId ON DELETE CASCADE) then deletes R's steps with no contributor and no stage. Observed result: R has 0 steps, but RugCostTotal still holds StepCost=1000.00 and Total=1000.00. The Trash page (cost site 4) shows that stale total, and LedgerVerifier reports 4 mismatches. The total only becomes correct when R is restored.
confirmed.fix: Make the usage check see trashed rugs: use IgnoreQueryFilters, as ServiceProviderRepository.HasWorkHistoryAsync does, so the type is only deactivated. Alternatively, change the FK to Restrict. Either way, a fast-path save can then never cascade into a cost-source table.

votes.reason: I traced the code at d45368b and could not refute the finding. Nothing elsewhere stops the scenario. (1) The usage check in StepTypeService.cs:123 calls the generic Repository<T>.ListAsync. That method is a plain Set.Where(predicate).AsNoTracking() with no IgnoreQueryFilters, and DI binds every IRepository<> to it (Infrastructure/DependencyInjection.cs:39). The RugWorkflowStep query filter `s.Rug.DeletedAt == null` (EntityConfigurations.cs:366) therefore hides steps on trashed rugs. If the type is also absent from every template, both counts are 0, and line 136 hard-deletes the ProcessStepType. (2) FK_RugWorkflowSteps_ProcessStepTypes_ProcessStepTypeId is ON DELETE CASCADE (InitialCreate.cs:231-235; the snapshot also shows Cascade). No later migration changes it, and nothing else references RugWorkflowSteps, so the database deletes the trashed rug's steps without objection. (3) The save takes the fast path. LedgerPass.SaveChangesAsync (LedgerPass.cs:54-57) calls SaveWithoutPassAsync when no entry is a watched type. The registered contributors and guards watch only Rug, RugPurchaseLine, RugWorkflowStep, RugSale, TenantPreferences and Tenant (LedgerModule.cs:31-37), not ProcessStepType or AuditLog. No contributor runs, so no RugCostTotal recompute happens. (4) The stale row is visible. UpsertCostTotalsAsync does not skip trashed rugs, so R's RugCostTotal still holds the step cost. RugRepository.ListDeletedAsync shows `r.CostTotal.Total` on the Trash page (site 4). LedgerRepository.ListRugIdsAsync (:215-225) includes trashed rugs. CostSql.StepCostOfRug reads RugWorkflowSteps with raw SQL, so its expected value is now 0, and LedgerVerifier reports mismatches. (5) This is a Phase 2 regression. At 2b5870c, the Trash page computed the total live from r.WorkflowSteps (SpecializedRepositories.cs:285-311), so the same cascade could not leave a stale number. The phase's switch to the stored RugCostTotal introduced the drift. The spec's risk table says a principal delete that cascades in the database must not bypass the pass. Severity is low: it needs a tenant step type used only on trashed rugs and in no template, and a restore re-runs RugImpact and heals the total.

confirmed.title: «به‌روزرسانی بهای تمام‌شده» writes CostAtSale from a value cached before the lock, with no version check
confirmed.scenario: RefreshCostAtSaleAsync loads the rug, and GetWithWorkflowAsync preloads RugCostTotal (Total = 10,000,000) into IRugCostTotalReader before any lock is taken. A concurrent request then completes a 500,000 step on the same sold rug and commits; the stored Total is now 10,500,000. The refresh request sets `sale.CostAtSale` from the cached 10,000,000 and saves. Its pass has an empty impact: SaleImpactContributor ignores a Modified sale unless RugId changes, and the rug row is untouched. Neither RugSale nor the rug row gives an xmin conflict, so the stale snapshot commits. Right after the user explicitly refreshed, the chip still reads cost changed after sale +500,000, and ActualProfit is wrong. The reverse order loses data too: a concurrent PUT sale edit calls `sales.Update(sale)` (:80), which marks every RugSale column modified, and overwrites a just-committed refresh with the old CostAtSale.
confirmed.fix: Have the pass write the refresh, as D.4 does for new sales. For example, a contributor or flag adds the rug to Impact.SaleAddedRugs, or a dedicated 'resnapshot' set, so RugCostTotalStage writes CostAtSale from the Total it computes under the lock. Also stop `sales.Update(sale)` on a tracked sale so an edit does not rewrite CostAtSale/CostAtSaleAt.

votes.reason: Only half of the finding holds. The stale-cache half (a concurrent step lands between the refresh's load and its save) does not cause a defect. The stored state it leaves is the same as running the refresh first and the step second, so the "cost changed after sale" chip and the snapshot-based ActualProfit are both correct. The reverse-order half is a real lost update, and I reproduced it on Postgres at d45368b. A sale edit (PUT) that loaded the sale before a refresh committed writes the old CostAtSale and CostAtSaleAt back over the refresh. Nothing detects this: RugSale has no xmin, the refresh never touches the Rugs row so the rug's xmin check in the edit passes, and both saves only take the tenant advisory lock after loading. The user who pressed refresh got a 200 with the new cost and an audit entry, but the stored snapshot quietly reverts. Severity is low because the window is only the edit request's server-side load-to-save time (it can also be waiting on the advisory lock while the refresh's save holds it).
votes.evidence:
Code at d45368b:
- RugSaleService.cs:122-139: RefreshCostAtSaleAsync sets sale.CostAtSale from workflowEngine.CalculateRugCosts(rug), which reads the per-request IRugCostTotalReader cache (WorkflowEngine.cs:319). RugRepository.cs:55 preloaded that cache at load time, before any lock.
- RugSaleService.cs:80: SaveAsync calls `sales.Update(sale)` on the already-tracked sale. Repository.cs:30 is `Set.Update(entity)`, which marks every RugSale column Modified, including CostAtSale and CostAtSaleAt. ChangeSetBuilder.cs:13-14 admits that Update() on a loaded graph marks everything Modified.
- EntityConfigurations.cs (RugSaleConfiguration, around line 293) has no xmin or concurrency token for RugSale. Only Rug has xmin, and the refresh does not modify the rug.
- SaleImpactContributor.cs:32 ignores a Modified sale unless RugId changed, so the refresh's pass has an empty impact and writes nothing under the lock. No save interceptors exist.

Reproduction: an integration test in a throwaway snapshot with a rugs_rv_* database (dropped afterwards; snapshot folder deleted).
- Setup: rug with a 1,000,000 purchase line, sold (CostAtSale = 1,000,000), then the line was raised to 1,500,000, so Total = 1,500,000.
- Scope C loaded the rug through GetWithWorkflowAsync. Scope A ran RefreshCostAtSaleAsync, and the stored value became (1,500,000, 1,500,000). Scope C then ran SaveAsync to edit the buyer name.
- Result: stored CostAtSale went back to 1,000,000 while Total stayed 1,500,000. The refresh was lost.

The stale-cache variant also reproduced: the refresh stored 1,500,000 while Total was 2,000,000. As explained above, that end state matches a serial refresh-then-step order, so it is not a defect on its own.

votes.reason:
I could not refute either part of the finding, and both reproduced against real Postgres. Severity is low because each needs a race of a few milliseconds. RefreshCostAtSaleAsync (RugSaleService.cs:122-139 at d45368b) reads the cost total before the tenant ledger lock. It loads the rug through GetWithWorkflowAsync (RugRepository.cs:40-56), which preloads RugCostTotal into the per-request IRugCostTotalReader cache with no lock and no transaction. Line 132 then sets sale.CostAtSale = workflowEngine.CalculateRugCosts(rug).TotalInvestment, and CalculateRugCosts (WorkflowEngine.cs:315-326) returns that cached stored.Total. The lock is taken only later, inside LedgerPass.SaveChangesAsync (LedgerPass.cs:126-127, LedgerSession.cs:56-71), and nothing re-reads the total afterwards.

In that pass, SaleImpactContributor (SaleImpactContributor.cs:32) ignores a Modified sale unless RugId changed. The impact is empty, so RugCostTotalStage and SnapshotCostAtSaleAsync never run, and the flush is a plain UPDATE of RugSales. RugSale has no xmin row version (EntityConfigurations.cs:291-322), and the refresh does not touch the rug row, so no concurrency conflict can fire. A cost change committed after the preload is therefore silently left out of the refreshed snapshot.

The reverse order loses data as well. SaveAsync calls sales.Update(sale) at line 80, which is Repository.Update => Set.Update (Repository.cs:30). On a tracked sale that marks every column modified, so an edit that loaded the sale before a refresh committed writes the old CostAtSale and CostAtSaleAt back after it. Nothing in the code resets IsModified and there is no SaveChanges interceptor.

confirmed.title: Restore blocked by a serial already in use shows an empty serial in the 409 message
confirmed.scenario: Reproduced on a throwaway DB. Rug X has serial «500» and is trashed. A new rug is saved with «500». Restoring X sets DeletedAt=null, so the flush violates the partial unique index IX_Rugs_TenantId_SerialNo. ChangedSerial() (:201) only returns rugs that are Added or whose SerialNo changed. The restored rug is Modified with an unchanged SerialNo, so it returns null and the exception is built with Serial="". Observed: SerialOverlapException with serial=[] and the message «شمارهٔ «» مال فرش دیگری است.». RugsController.Restore shows that message as the toast on the Trash page, and nextFree=501 is attached even though it is irrelevant to a restore.
confirmed.fix: In ChangedSerial(), also return the serial of a Rug whose DeletedAt went from non-null to null (restored), or fall back to the serial of any Modified or Added rug with a SerialNo. Better still, look up the colliding rug by (TenantId, SerialNo) so ConflictingSerial is filled.

votes.reason: The finding is real. I traced it at d45368b and nothing upstream stops it. The restore path never fills in the serial, so the 409 message names an empty serial. Two rugs with the same serial text break the unique index during the flush. That happens before SerialOverlapStage can run, which is the only code that would give a message with real serials. ChangedSerial() then skips the restored rug, because the rug is only Modified and its SerialNo has not changed. The message comes out as «شمارهٔ «» مال فرش دیگری است.» and the Trash page shows it as the toast. Severity is low: the save is still correctly blocked and rolled back, and only the message is wrong.
votes.evidence:
Code path at d45368b:

1. **Restore loads and changes the rug.**
   - `RugManagementService.RestoreAsync` (src/RugsManagment.Application/Services/RugManagementService.cs:421-432) loads the rug through `GetDeletedAsync`.
   - That query is tracked: it uses `IgnoreQueryFilters` and has no `AsNoTracking` (src/RugsManagment.Infrastructure/Persistence/Repositories/RugRepository.cs:504-508).
   - It then sets only `DeletedAt=null`, `DeletedByUserId=null` and `UpdatedAt`, and calls `unitOfWork.SaveChangesAsync` with no outer transaction. The pre-check comment at :417-419 says the ledger pass will give a 409.

2. **The pass runs, but the flush fails first.**
   - `Rug` is watched by `RugImpactContributor`, so the pass is not skipped.
   - The contributor adds the restored rug to `SerialCheckRugs` (src/RugsManagment.Application/Ledger/Contributors/RugImpactContributor.cs:63-69).
   - But `SerialOverlapStage` only runs after `session.FlushAsync` (src/RugsManagment.Application/Ledger/LedgerPass.cs:66-73).
   - The flush violates the partial unique index `IX_Rugs_TenantId_SerialNo`, which is filtered on `"DeletedAt" IS NULL AND "SerialNo" IS NOT NULL` (src/RugsManagment.Infrastructure/Persistence/Configurations/EntityConfigurations.cs:98-100). The other active rug has the same SerialNo text.

3. **The exception is built with an empty serial.**
   - `LedgerSession.SaveAsync` catches the unique violation for that index and throws `new SerialOverlapException(ChangedSerial() ?? string.Empty, conflictingSerial: null, nextFree: null, ex)` (src/RugsManagment.Infrastructure/Persistence/Ledger/LedgerSession.cs:192-195).
   - `ChangedSerial()` (:201-208) only returns Rug entries that are `Added`, or `Modified` with `OriginalValue(SerialNo) != SerialNo`.
   - The restored rug is Modified with an unchanged SerialNo, and no other Rug entry is tracked, so it returns null and `Serial = ""`.

4. **The message names no serial.**
   - `BuildMessage` uses `TakenMessage` because `other` is null (src/RugsManagment.Application/Ledger/SerialOverlapException.cs:26, 52-57). The result is «شمارهٔ «» مال فرش دیگری است.».

5. **nextFree is added even though it does not help a restore.**
   - The transaction is Owned, so `LedgerPass` catches the error and rethrows `overlap.WithNextFree(...)` (LedgerPass.cs:89-94).

6. **The user sees it as the Trash toast.**
   - `RugsController.Restore` catches `DomainConflictException` and calls `PageToast.SetError(TempData, ex.Message)`, then redirects to Trash (src/RugsManagment.Web/Controllers/RugsController.cs:132-136).

**Concrete case:** trash a rug with serial 500, create a new rug with serial 500, then restore the trashed one. The toast reads «شمارهٔ «» مال فرش دیگری است.»

**Test coverage:** the existing test `RestoringARug_RechecksItsSerial` (tests/RugsManagment.IntegrationTests/Ledger/LedgerPassIntegrationTests.cs:263-287) only asserts that the exception type is thrown, so it does not catch the empty serial.

**When it happens:** only when the two serials are the exact same text. If the serials only overlap as ranges, the index is not violated and `SerialOverlapStage` gives a full message.

votes.reason:
The finding holds. I traced it through the code at d45368b. I did not build anything or run it against a database; the trace is deterministic.

When a restored rug's serial now belongs to an active rug with the exact same text, the 409 is raised by the unique index during the flush, not by SerialOverlapStage. LedgerSession builds that exception from ChangedSerial(), which skips a restored rug because its SerialNo did not change. The serial therefore comes back as "", and the Trash page toast reads «شمارهٔ «» مال فرش دیگری است.».

Severity is low. The restore is still refused correctly with a 409 and the rug stays in the trash. Only the message is broken: it does not say which serial is taken.
votes.evidence:
The trace, all at d45368b:

1. **Index.** EntityConfigurations.cs:98-100 and migration 20261004063353_RugModelV2AndCosting.cs:233-238 create IX_Rugs_TenantId_SerialNo, unique on (TenantId, SerialNo), filtered to `"DeletedAt" IS NULL AND "SerialNo" IS NOT NULL`. A trashed rug therefore frees its serial: a new rug can be saved with «500», and the overlap query at LedgerRepository.cs:56 also ignores deleted rugs.

2. **Restore.** RugManagementService.RestoreAsync (:421-432):
   - It loads the rug tracked, via GetDeletedAsync (RugRepository.cs:504-508, IgnoreQueryFilters, no AsNoTracking).
   - It sets only DeletedAt, DeletedByUserId and UpdatedAt, never SerialNo.
   - It calls unitOfWork.SaveChangesAsync, which goes to LedgerPass.SaveChangesAsync (UnitOfWork.cs:21-22).

3. **Pass order.** RugImpactContributor.cs:63-69 adds the restored rug to SerialCheckRugs. However, SerialOverlapStage only runs after the flush (LedgerPass.cs:66-73). The flush, `session.FlushAsync` → LedgerSession.SaveAsync at :186, sends an UPDATE that sets DeletedAt to NULL. That UPDATE violates the partial unique index first (SqlState 23505, constraint IX_Rugs_TenantId_SerialNo), so the stage never runs.

4. **The defect.** LedgerSession.cs:194-195 builds `new SerialOverlapException(ChangedSerial() ?? string.Empty, conflictingSerial: null, nextFree: null, ex)`. ChangedSerial() (:201-208) returns only rugs that are Added, or Modified with SerialNo OriginalValue different from the current value. The restored rug is Modified with an unchanged SerialNo, and no other Rug is in the tracker, so it returns null and Serial becomes "".

5. **Message.** BuildMessage (SerialOverlapException.cs:52-57) uses TakenMessage when `other` is null, producing «شمارهٔ «» مال فرش دیگری است.». LedgerPass.cs:89-94 then rethrows `overlap.WithNextFree(nextFree)`, which copies the empty Serial (:46-47) and attaches the tenant-wide nextFree.

6. **UI.** RugsController.Restore (:132-136) catches the DomainConflictException and calls `PageToast.SetError(TempData, ex.Message)`, then redirects to Trash. The user sees the empty serial.

7. **Tests.** No test covers a restore that hits this index. LedgerContributorTests.Restore_RechecksTheSerial_TrashDoesNot (:101) only checks that the rug lands in SerialCheckRugs.

confirmed.title: Step-cost preview ignores lot quantity and the Priced* snapshot, so 'final cost' is wrong for lots
confirmed.scenario: Preview() prices one piece on whatever W/L the caller sends. PricingPreviewRequest has no quantity and no snapshot, and RugWorkflowPanel.vue:374 passes the rug's effective widthMeters/lengthMeters. The step itself is saved through CalculateStepCost/StepLinePrice as piece x PricedQuantity on the Priced* size. Verified on a throwaway DB: lot «3911 - 3960» x50 at 0.40x0.40, PerSquareMeter 85,000 with a -10,000 discount. The editor shows base 13,600 and 'هزینهٔ نهایی' 3,600. Saving gives CalculatedCost 680,000 and effective cost 670,000. The floor at 0 is also applied to the piece instead of the line, so a discount the preview shows as clamping to 0 is not clamped after save. Second case: a single rug priced at intake 2.08x2.10 (4.37 m²) and later given a final size of 2.00x2.00. A rate change previews 90,000 x 4.00 = 360,000 but saves 90,000 x 4.37 = 393,300.
confirmed.fix: Add Quantity (and optional priced L/W) to PricingPreviewRequest. Have the panel send the step's PricedLength/PricedWidth/PricedQuantity, or the rug's quantity when the step has no snapshot. Compute the base with RugCostMath.StepLinePrice and apply StepEffectiveCost to the line amount. Show the piece price as 'piece x qty'.

votes.reason: I could not refute the finding. At d45368b, the step-cost preview prices a single piece on whatever size the client sends. The real save prices the whole line (piece price x PricedQuantity) on the Priced* snapshot and applies the adjustment and the floor at 0 to that line. Nothing in the editor, panel, controller or service makes up the difference, and the code's own comments say the preview and the saved step give the same number. Phase 2 introduced the gap: at 2b5870c, CalculateStepCost and Preview both priced one piece on the rug's size. Phase 2 added the snapshot and the x qty rule to CalculateStepCost only (spec D.3, "Step pricing on lots").
votes.evidence:
Preview, in src/RugsManagment.Application/Services/CostCalculationService.cs:
- Lines 90 and 99 call RugCostMath.StepPiecePrice with r.LengthMeters and r.WidthMeters. There is no quantity.
- Line 105 is `RugCostMath.StepEffectiveCost(baseCost, null, r.Adjustment)`, so the floor at 0 is applied to the single piece.
- PricingPreviewRequest (src/RugsManagment.Application/DTOs/Pricing/PricingDtos.cs:6-13) has no Quantity field and no Priced* fields.
- PricingApiController.Preview passes the request straight through.

Save path:
- Advance and pricing saves go through WorkflowEngine.cs:129/161 to PriceAsync (WorkflowEngine.cs:363-377).
- PriceAsync takes a snapshot only when there is none, or when RefreshPricedSize is set: `step.SnapshotPricingSize(rug.LengthMeters, rug.WidthMeters, Math.Max(1, rug.Quantity))`.
- CalculateStepCost (CostCalculationService.cs:46-50) then uses PricedLength/PricedWidth/PricedQuantity, and ComputeBase calls RugCostMath.StepLinePrice, which is piece x qty (RugCostMath.cs:210-213).
- The adjustment and the floor are applied later to the line through StepEffectiveCost (RugCostMath.cs:219-220).

Client:
- RugWorkflowPanel.vue:374 passes only `:width="rug?.widthMeters" :length="rug?.lengthMeters"` (one piece, effective size).
- CostRuleEditor.vue:220-227 posts only width, length, model, rate, combinedJson, manualCost and adjustment. It shows preview.total as "هزینهٔ نهایی" at line 310 and never multiplies by quantity.
- The panel never sends refreshPricedSize (movePayload, lines 181-193), so an existing snapshot is always kept.
- Nothing stops a lot (Quantity > 1) from having workflow steps.

Lot example (traced by hand: 0.40 x 0.40, qty 50, PerSquareMeter 85,000, discount -10,000):
- Preview: round(0.16 x 85,000) = 13,600, total 3,600.
- Saved: CalculatedCost 13,600 x 50 = 680,000, effective 670,000.
- With a 20,000 discount, the preview clamps to 0 but the saved line is 660,000.

Final-size example: the snapshot was taken at intake 2.08 x 2.10, and the final size is later set to 2.00 x 2.00.
- The preview uses 4.00 m².
- The save keeps the 4.37 m² snapshot, because the panel never asks for a refresh.

confirmed.title: Serial inputs use inputmode="numeric", so iPhone users cannot type a lot range or a text serial; the manual lot split cannot be completed
confirmed.scenario: Lot «3911 - 3960» with quantity 45 (range longer than quantity), so automatic=false and both «شمارهٔ بخشی که می‌ماند» and «شمارهٔ بخش جداشده» are required. On iOS Safari, inputmode="numeric" opens the digits-only number pad, which has no '-', space or letters. «3911 - 3930» (and «۳۹۱۱ تا ۳۹۳۰») cannot be typed, so the split cannot be done from the phone. The same keypad on the RugForm serial (RugForm.vue:429) makes text serials like «A-12» untypeable.
confirmed.fix: Use inputmode="text" (or omit inputmode) on serial inputs, or add a «تا» helper button and a separate from/to number pair that builds the range.

votes.reason: The finding holds, at low severity. At d45368b, RugSplit.island.vue:163 and :176 put inputmode="numeric" on the two serial inputs, and nothing else in the dialog can fill them. They are shown when automatic=false: the lot's range is longer than its quantity, or the lot has a text serial. In that case the server requires both values. WebKit on iOS maps inputmode="numeric" to the digits-only number pad on iPhone (0-9, no '-', no space, no letters, no way to switch layout). So a range or text serial cannot be typed there. Digits alone give a single number covering one piece, which the server rejects for any part bigger than one piece. The split can only be finished on an iPhone by pasting text in. The spec itself says serial inputs should use inputmode="text" (G.1). RugForm.vue:429 has the same problem for text serials like A-12 and ranges longer than the quantity. Ranges equal to the quantity are covered there by the dasteh-kon helper button.
votes.evidence:
RugSplit.island.vue (d45368b) lines 159-184: both serial inputs have `inputmode="numeric"`, with placeholders "3911 - 3940" and "3941 - 3960", so a range with a separator is expected. No helper button builds the range. The fields are shown only when `!automatic`, and `automatic` (lines 56-60) is false when the lot is not a range exactly as long as its quantity.

RugSplitService.cs:151-168 (`Plan`): if both serials are empty and the range is not exactly as long as the quantity, it throws `ForField("serialTo", SplitSerialsRequired)`. `ReadTyped` then requires `serial.Covers(quantity)`.

SerialNumber.cs: `Covers` is `!IsNumeric || Count >= quantity`. A digits-only entry like "3911" parses as a single number with Count 1. A range needs '-', one of the other dash characters, '_' or "تا" (Persian "to") as separator (`TryReadSeparator`), plus optional spaces. None of these is on the iPhone number pad. So the scenario fails: lot 3911-3960 with quantity 45, take 20, kept part 25 needs "3911 - 3935"; typing "3911" gives E_SERIAL_QTY.

Spec final-spec.md:1541 (G.1) says GridCell uses "`numeric` for int, `text` for serial", so the spec intends serial inputs to use a text keyboard.

RugForm.vue:429 has the same `inputmode="numeric"` on the serial field. Its hint "مثل ۳۷۷۸، یا برای دسته ۳۹۱۱ - ۳۹۶۰" ("like 3778, or for a lot 3911 - 3960") expects a range. The dasteh-kon and benevis helpers (lines 438-443) only cover a range exactly as long as the quantity. Text serials (allowed by G.4, e.g. A-12) and longer ranges cannot be typed on iPhone.

votes.reason:
This defect is real, and low severity as reported. Both serial inputs in the manual split dialog (RugSplit.island.vue:163 and :176) and the RugForm serial input (RugForm.vue:429) are text fields for serials, but they set inputmode="numeric". Since iOS 13, an iPhone shows its digits-only number pad for that mode, with no '-', no space and no way to switch to letters. A web search result says this, and MDN only promises digits 0-9.

The manual split cannot work with digits alone:
- The dialog asks for both serials when the lot cannot be numbered automatically (RugSplit.island.vue:56-60). That happens when the range is longer than the quantity or the serial is text.
- The server then requires each serial to cover its part's quantity (RugSplitService.cs:163-164 and :185-189). So a kept part of 25 or more pieces needs a range.
- SerialNumber.TryParse accepts a range only with a separator: '-', '–', '_' or «تا» (SerialNumber.cs:12, 19-20). Digits alone parse as a single number, which covers 1 piece and is rejected with the quantity error.

So on an iPhone the user cannot finish this split. Pasting is the only way around it, which a non-technical user is unlikely to find. RugForm has a «دسته کن» button (serialAsLot) that covers lots whose range equals the quantity. It does not help with a range longer than the quantity or a text serial like «A-12»: letters and '-' cannot be typed there either.

Both files were added or changed in this phase (diff 2b5870c..d45368b). The spec's own rule for grid serial cells (G.1, final-spec.md:1541) uses inputmode "text" for serials, which shows the numeric choice here is a mistake. iPad keyboards (numbers-and-punctuation) and Android Gboard (which has '-' and space) are not affected.

RugSplit.island.vue@d45368b:
- 157: `<div v-if="!automatic">`, and both inputs are required.
- 163 and 176: `inputmode="numeric"`. The placeholders are "3911 - 3940" and "3941 - 3960", so ranges are expected.
- 56-60: automatic only when `r.to - r.from + 1 === props.quantity`.

RugSplitService.cs@d45368b:
- 151-160: when both serials are empty and the range does not equal the quantity, it throws E_SPLIT_SERIALS.
- 163-164 and 185-189: each typed serial must Cover its part's quantity.

SerialNumber.cs@d45368b:
- 12: the accepted range forms are "3911 - 3960", "3911–3960", "3911_3960" and "3911 تا 3960".
- 19-20: "3911 3960" is a format error.
- So a range cannot be written with digits only.

RugForm.vue@d45368b:
- 429: `inputmode="numeric"`, while the hint at 424 asks for «۳۹۱۱ - ۳۹۶۰».
- serialAsLot only builds start..start+qty-1, so text serials and ranges longer than the quantity still need typing.

final-spec.md:1541: GridCell uses "`text` for serial".

Platform behaviour, from a web search result: "iOS 13 updated inputmode=numeric to use the numeric keypad without punctuation". MDN: "only requires the digits 0–9. Devices may or may not show a minus key."

Scenario: lot «3911 - 3960» with quantity 45, split off 20 on iOS Safari. The keypad gives only 0-9. Typing "39113935" gives a format/quantity error, and "3911" gives E_SERIAL_QTY, so the split cannot be completed.

Both files were added or changed in diff 2b5870c..d45368b. I did not test on a physical iPhone; the iOS keyboard behaviour comes from that web search result rather than a device test.

rejected.title: LedgerPass leaves its nested-pass flag set when BeginAsync throws, so every later save in the scope fails
rejected.why:
The code does what the finding says: LedgerPass.cs:59 sets `_running = true` before `session.BeginAsync` at :60, and both lines are outside the try/finally. So in theory the flag can stay set. But the failure scenario cannot happen in the shipped code at d45368b.

LedgerPass is scoped (LedgerModule.cs:25). Only one production caller keeps using the same scope after a failed save: TenantSeedRunner.SeedAllTenantsAsync. In that caller, neither way BeginAsync could throw is reachable:

1. **Cancelled token.** The per-tenant catch at TenantSeedRunner.cs:67 is `when (ex is not OperationCanceledException)`. A cancellation leaves the loop altogether, so no later tenant ever meets the stuck flag.
2. **Non-cancellation exception from the owned-transaction path.** `db.Database.BeginTransactionAsync` (LedgerSession.cs:49) would have to do network I/O and fail. It doesn't do I/O here:
   - Just before the save, the seed contributors run queries on the same DbContext (TenantPreferencesSeedContributor.cs:18, CostCategorySeedContributor.cs:82 and :102). Those return an idle connector to the Npgsql pool.
   - Startup runs before `app.Run` (Program.cs:282) and there are no hosted services, so nothing else takes that connector in the meantime.
   - Npgsql hands out an idle pooled connector without a round trip, and sends BEGIN only with the next command. That next command is LockTenantAsync inside the try, so a dropped connection fails there and the finally resets the flag.

The savepoint path (CreateSavepointAsync, which does I/O) only runs inside ExecuteInTransactionAsync. Its single caller is RugManagementService.cs:213, and it lets the exception end the request, so that scope is thrown away. The only other code that catches save errors and continues is the DuplicateKeyException/Reset handling, also in TenantSeedRunner. No production path catches a save failure and saves again in the same scope after BeginAsync throws.

The reviewer's reproduction used a test-only sequence (cancelled token, manual uow.Reset(), another save in the same scope) that no production code performs. | The code does what the reviewer says: at LedgerPass.cs:59-60, `_running = true` is set before `session.BeginAsync` and outside the try/finally. But the claimed impact needs code that catches a failed save and then keeps saving in the same DI scope, and that path can't be reached at d45368b. TenantSeedRunner is the only code that catches a failed save and keeps saving in the same scope. It can't get a non-cancellation exception out of BeginAsync, and it doesn't catch cancellation. Every other caller lets the exception end the request or scope.
